about: Editorial scores for what each book is good FOR. skill 0-10: does it contain runnable frameworks, procedures a person executes this week. video 0-10: does it carry narrative, a turn, concrete detail, a scene worth watching. These are judgments about the books, not measurements of the extracted text. Books not listed here are unscored, not zero.

scored.why: Mental models and inversion, stated as usable checklists. Munger is already a guide and installs nothing.
Drucker on managing yourself. Manage time before tasks, organise around contribution, first things first.
A book about procedure that is itself a procedure, with surgical and aviation stories to carry it.
Six principles, each with a named mechanism and a countermeasure. Among the most directly runnable books written.
Separate people from problem, interests not positions, invent options, insist on criteria. A negotiation procedure.
Grove on managerial leverage, one to ones, and output as a measurable quantity.
A hundred lenses, each a question you point at a design. The densest framework book on the shelf.
Explicit algorithms for real decisions: when to stop looking, how to sort, when to explore.

scored.match: the score takes care of itself
scored.why: Walsh's Standard of Performance, plus the story of applying it to a team that had just gone 2 and 14.
Strategy canvas and the four actions framework. Draw it, then act on what the drawing shows.
Habit stacking, make it obvious and easy, systems over goals. Built to be executed.
Scheduled blocks and ruthless elimination of shallow work, aimed at the modern knowledge worker.
A complete capture and review system. All method, no narrative.
The grand slam offer, built as a formula you fill in. Hormozi is the roster's missing go to market voice.
Dalio's decision rules plus the story of the bet that nearly ended him. Already a guide with one skill.
One idea applied relentlessly to time, customers, and effort.
A staged playbook for network effects, with the hard early phase treated seriously.
Hopkins on testing, headlines, and measurement. A century old and still operational.
Self 1 and Self 2, which transfers far outside sport, with vivid coaching scenes.
Positioning laws stated as rules you can check a plan against.
Taleb on asymmetry and who bears the downside. Taleb is a guide with one skill.
The fragile, robust, antifragile triad, usable on any system you own. Note the extraction looks thin.
Tail risk and the narrative fallacy, with the arguments that made Taleb's name.
A compressed start something procedure, aimed at the reader who has not begun.
Ferriss on elimination, automation, and defining the one thing. Meta-productivity as method.
One rule applied without exception, which is why it works and why it is teachable.
Leverage, specific knowledge, and judgement. Naval is a guide who installs nothing.
Chouinard's operating philosophy, carried by the story of building it against every convention.
The best pure narrative on the shelf. Near ruin repeatedly, concrete scenes, a real voice.
An anecdote machine. Every chapter is already an episode with a turn and a punchline.
Isaacson's biography. Jobs is a guide who installs nothing, and this is the source for both paths.
The fullest text on the shelf for a guide we already have. Ledger A, the Cleveland Massacre, the dimes.
Isaacson again. The notebooks give concrete, filmable detail that most biographies lack.
A thesis carried entirely by narrative. The method is visible through the story rather than listed.
Isaacson. Elon is a guide already, so this deepens rather than starts.
The PayPal mafia, which is a story about a group rather than a person, and rare for that.
A sequence of decisive moments, which is the natural shape of an episode series.
Jensen is a guide who installs nothing. Near death, the CUDA bet, thirty days from going out of business.
Michael Dell on the going private fight. A single high stakes arc.
The largest life on the shelf with no guide yet. Enormous turns, and 371k words of text.
Rubin in short sections that are almost pre-cut into episodes.

scored.match: the hero with a thousand faces
scored.why: Campbell's monomyth, which is both a framework and inherently narrative.
Already a guide and a registered source. Practices plus the strangeness of a emperor writing to himself.
Seneca is a guide with two skills. The letters are short and self contained, which suits episodes.
Same material, Ferriss's packaging. Useful if the other extraction is thin.
Already a registered source for Seneca with a skill attached.
Deutsch is a guide with a full book page. Hard to vary is a genuinely usable test.
Deutsch's first book, already registered, currently one skill and no episodes.
Would make an unusual and very good series, and almost nobody has done it well on video.
Dense and difficult. High effort to do honestly, and Peterson carries real landmines.
One distinction, applied everywhere, with the studies that established it.
Givers, takers, matchers. A clean typology with research behind it.
Deliberate practice, specified precisely enough to actually do.
Zinsser on cutting. Rules you can apply to a paragraph immediately.
Maximiser and satisficer, plus a practical case for constraining your own options.
One distinction that reframes everything. Short, aphoristic, well suited to short episodes.
A prediction book, best treated as an argument to examine rather than a manual.
Balaji, free online, and directly relevant to the community around this project.
Compiled Balaji, easier to mine for discrete ideas than the book.
Lee Kuan Yew is a guide with two skills and this registered source is 260k words unused.
Lee in his own blunt voice, which is the hardest thing to fake and the best thing to clone.
Lee assessing the world late in life. Opinionated and quotable.
Public domain, foundational, no guide yet. A serious undertaking at 386k words.
Public domain and already in dialogue form, which is unusually close to a script.
The trial and death of Socrates. Public domain, and the most dramatic philosophy ever written.
411k words of Plotinus. Enormous effort, very narrow audience.
Dawkins. The gene's eye view is a genuine reframe, and memes originate here.
Cumulative selection explained better than almost anywhere else.
Pollan. Strong narrative, but the subject needs care in a public series.

scored.match: the 7 principles for making marriage work
scored.why: Gottman. Research backed and unusually procedural for a relationships book.
Eight structured conversations. Literally a set of instructions.
Already has seven episodes and zero skills, which is backwards for a book this procedural.
Done. Five episodes shipped.
Strong narrative, but under copyright and the only local copies came from a shadow library.
567k words of novel with a thesis. Enormous, and politically loaded.
As above. Narrative is strong, the framing is contentious.
Public domain and one of the great psychological narratives. No obvious guide fit.
818k words. Doing this respectfully is a project, not a task.
The largest text on the shelf. Same caution.
413k words of Mises. Rigorous and forbidding, with a narrow audience.
Sowell explaining mechanisms clearly. Good for diagrams if the shot vocabulary gets built.
Very short, very quotable, and each chapter is close to an episode already.
A contrarian parenting argument, unusual on this shelf and thinly covered elsewhere.
Sivers in short chapters. The natural episode length is already the chapter length.
Sivers again. Short, concrete, and each lesson is a scene.
A leaving the career narrative that a lot of readers are currently living.
Ferriss on meta learning. The learning method matters more than the recipes.
duplicate guard
John Mackey, who is already a guide with one skill and no episodes.
Compiled Elon, already a registered source, currently pending.
Short and procedural. The five step algorithm is here and Elon already has skills.
Hoffman. Career as a startup, with usable planning frameworks.
Gil on scaling. Operational and specific, aimed at a real job.
Inflections and insights, from the Floodgate approach to early stage.
Godin. One idea, sharply stated, easy to act on.
Funnels laid out as procedure. Dated in places, still operational.

scored.match: the art of selling to the affluent
scored.why: Specific sales procedure for a specific buyer.
Self examination methods, adjacent to the Vervaeke material already on the site.
De Mello in very short pieces, which suits the episode format almost exactly.
Morning pages and artist dates. A twelve week programme, entirely runnable.
Kondo's method applied to work. Same single rule as the original.
Pieter Levels on shipping fast and staying small. Practical and opinionated.
Visakan on agency and building in public. Short sections, high energy.
Career decision frameworks, worked through carefully at 127k words.
Popper. Rigorous and long, and the fallibilism connects to Deutsch who is already a guide.
